description: List the documented OEM replacement parts for one known laptop model. Use it once you know the model; call resolve_request first for a vague request, get_part or get_part_fits when you start from a part number, and get_coverage only to see which part types exist. model accepts a slug or a full name; an ambiguous name (e.g. "T14") returns status ambiguous with candidates and no parts, so ask the user and call again with the slug; an unknown model is an error result. type keeps only parts whose type equals it, case-insensitive. Paging: with neither limit nor cursor you get every part in one response. With either, you get one page; follow next_cursor until it is null. With 2+ documented screens, panel_options says how they differ, so tell the user to check their current panel's part number or connector. A type with no parts returns parts [] and fit_status no_documented_fit: no document, not incompatibility. Read-only.

client.description: Optional: your agent or app name (letters and digits), used only for anonymous usage counts.

cursor.description: Optional. The next_cursor value from the previous page, e.g. "25".

limit.description: Optional page size, 1 to 100; default 25, or 50 with view compact.

model.description: Required. Model slug or full name, e.g. "lenovo-thinkpad-t490" or "ThinkPad T490".

view.description: Optional. full (default) includes buy_links and source details; compact keeps part number, type, confidence, lpf_url, constraints and source_url.

name: get_model_parts

fit_status.description: Present when there is no fit or no result: LPF has no OEM document for it. Never means incompatible.

display_name.description: Short human label; not an identifier

title: Get parts for a model
